name: Light Maroon
lede: Light Maroon is a muted raspberry-wine red, a lightened maroon, and the books use the same phrase for a different color.

sections.title: Maroon, lightened
sections.body:
Maroon began as a brown. St Clair gives the French *marron*, chestnut, as its root, with the color originally nut brown and now a brownish dark red [1]. This swatch is a lighter, pinker step along from that dark red, drawn in our library from the xkcd color survey [2]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[light-burgundy]], and [[raspberry]] is close too [2].

Paterson uses the phrase another way, describing FireBrick, one of the 140 colors in the X11 set, as a light maroon [3]. The two are different swatches: FireBrick is #B22222 and this is #A24857 [2][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Light Maroon is uncommon in painting [4]. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 27 (0.11 per cent) hold a color within six units of it over at least five per cent of the canvas [4]. Ten of the 27 date from the 1900s, 5.3 times the archive rate for that century [4]. They are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [4].
